newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif., Premier in talks on park.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif., Premier in talks on park.

text.p: The Vallejo, Calif., city council said it had entered exclusive negotiations with Premier Parks Inc to assume management of the financially-troubled Marine World Africa USA theme park.
The agreement, expected to be finalized over the next few weeks, would also include an option that would allow Oklahoma City-based Premier Parks to purchase the 100-acre attraction.
Under the initial terms of the proposed five year agreement, Premier Parks would assume management of the park within the next 60 to 90 days, the city said in a statement.
The city council voted in October to take over the park.

The city assumed control of the park and its debt in large part because the park was short about $2 million owed to noteholders on November 1. As part of the takeover, the city assumed about $52 million of long-term park debt.
Declining revenues and attendance have hurt the park financially. Attendance has fallen about 19 percent since 1995, when some 1.6 million visited the park.

City officials said the theme park, the largest private employer in the city, was an essential part of the local economy. The park has 1,300 employees during the summer season and about 500 employees year-round.
